issues.legal_issue: A female Hindu with a pre-existing interest in property that is partitioned and possessed by her becomes its full owner under the statutory conversion rule, even if the partition award describes her estate as restricted.
material_facts: Under the Hindu Women's Right to Property Act, the widow had an existing interest in her deceased husband's property and a right to seek partition, although her interest was limited.
An arbitration partition allocated specific properties to her and described her interest as a widow's estate; the award was made a court decree.
She possessed the allotted properties when the Hindu Succession Act came into force.
A suit sought to restrain her from alienating the properties on the basis that she remained a limited owner.
issues.conclusion: The widow became the full owner of the allotted properties under Section 14(1); the partition award and decree did not bring the case within Section 14(2) because the allotment gave effect to her pre-existing right.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1) and its Explanation cover property possessed by a female Hindu, including property acquired at partition, and “possessed” includes actual or constructive possession. Section 14(2) is an exception to subsection (1) and applies where property is acquired for the first time under a gift, instrument, decree, order, or award prescribing a restricted estate, without a pre-existing right. Under Sections 3(1)–(3) of the Hindu Women's Right to Property Act, the widow had an interest and a right to partition, though that interest was limited before the Hindu Succession Act. The Court relied on Gummalapura Taggina Matada Kotturuswami v. Setra Veerayya on the meaning of possession; S. S. Munna Lal v. S. S. Rajkumar on possession of a share declared by decree; Rangaswami Naicker v. Chinnammal on Section 14(2) preserving restrictions imposed on rights created for the first time; and Sukhram v. Gauri Shankar on conversion of a pre-existing limited interest into full ownership under Section 14(1).

rule.if: female_property_ownership_dispute and preexisting_interest_in_property and partitioned_to_realize_existing_interest and possessed_when_law_commenced

predicates.female_property_ownership_dispute: The proceeding disputes whether a female Hindu's interest in property is full ownership or a restricted estate.
predicates.preexisting_interest_in_property: The female Hindu had an interest in the property before it was allotted to her at partition.
predicates.partitioned_to_realize_existing_interest: The property was allotted to the female Hindu through a partition that gave effect to her existing interest.
predicates.possessed_when_law_commenced: The female Hindu possessed the property, actually or constructively, when the law providing for conversion of her interest came into force.

issues.definition: When the proceeding concerns a female Hindu's property ownership, she had a pre-existing interest that partition gave effect to, and she possessed the property when the law came into force, the rule means she became its full owner.
